ThingDef.label: The Art of Shin (心)
ThingDef.description:
A well worn hardcover tome, copied from an original manuscript found on a scorched planet. It pages are split by bookmarks and margins scrawled with ink. The text speaks of clearing the mind so that it may be sowed with the heaviest of recollections and serve as fertile ground for one's heart to bloom outward. It names this technique Shin (心), and claims that mastery over it allows one to match even shock marines in one-to-one combat through will alone. It sounds outlandish, but tempting. Its previous owner has documented the process of honing their heart on thorough annotations scrawled on every blank space available. They speak of enduring untold hardship, of risking life and limb without sparing a thought. The apathy in which they describe filling their mind with their worst moments during a raid is frankly chilling.

The tome further describes shaping the projection of one's resolve into Mang (望), rings of light that wrap around one's weapon or limbs and greatly increase their power. The annotator expresses frustrastion at manifesting a single ring after more than a year of practice and states they will document further developments. The rest of the book's margins are blank.

The text warns that, although the path offers powers unmatched; mastery will be an endless, perilous journey. Each step will only grow wider.
